newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee invulnerable to S.E. Asian crises - RBI.
newsitem.headline: India rupee invulnerable to S.E. Asian crises - RBI.

text.p: Financial crises in south east Asian economies are unlikely to have any fall-out on the rupee because India's trade with those countries is very limited, a senior central bank official said on Friday.

"It is unlikely that any turmoil in south east Asian economies would have a direct impact upon the Indian rupee as India's trade with the five countries of the region (Thailand, Malaysia, the Philippines and Singapore) constituted only 7.8 percent in 1996/97," Deputy Governor Y.V. Reddy of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said.
Financial year 1996/97 ran from April 96 to March 97.
Reddy was speaking to the 11th national assembly of the For of Goa.

He said these nations' currencies were more internationally traded, with a larger number of hedging products available. IN addition, the central banks of several south east Asian economies follow a pattern of pooling their resources to counter any attacks on their currencies.
"It is possible that the sentiments that govern the interest of investors in these countries are different from the sentiments of investors coming to India," Reddy added.
